landmarks.name: Lalibela Rock-Hewn Churches
landmarks.writeup: A group of 11 medieval monolithic churches carved out of rock, considered a pilgrimage site and a UNESCO World Heritage site.

wiki.extract: The eleven Rock-hewn Churches of Lalibela are monolithic churches located in the western Ethiopian Highlands near the town of Lalibela, named after the late-12th and early-13th century King Gebre Meskel Lalibela of the Zagwe dynasty, who commissioned the massive building project of 11 rock-hewn churches to recreate the holy city of Jerusalem in his own kingdom. The site remains in use by the Ethiopian Orthodox Christian Church to this day, and it remains an important place of pilgrimage for Ethiopian Orthodox worshipers. It took 24 years to build all the 11 rock hewn churches.

landmarks.name: Simien Mountains National Park
landmarks.writeup: Known for dramatic mountain scenery and endemic wildlife including the Ethiopian wolf and Gelada baboon.

wiki.extract: Simien Mountains National Park is the largest national park in Ethiopia. Located in the North Gondar Zone of the Amhara Region, its territory covers the highest parts of the Simien Mountains and includes Ras Dashan, the highest point in Ethiopia.

landmarks.name: Aksum Obelisks
landmarks.writeup: Ancient stelae marking the ruins of the Kingdom of Aksum, an important center of early Christianity.

wiki.extract: The Obelisk of Axum is a 4th-century CE, 24-metre (79 ft) tall phonolite stele, weighing 160 tonnes, in the city of Axum in Ethiopia. It is ornamented with two false doors at the base and features decorations resembling windows on all sides. The obelisk ends in a semi-circular top, which used to be enclosed by metal frames.

landmarks.name: The Blue Nile Falls
landmarks.writeup: A spectacular waterfall on the Blue Nile river, locally known as 'Tis Issat' meaning 'smoking water.'

wiki.extract: The Blue Nile is a river originating at Lake Tana in Ethiopia. It travels for approximately 1,450 km (900 mi) through Ethiopia and Sudan. Along with the White Nile, it is one of the two major tributaries of the Nile and supplies about 85.6% of the water to the Nile during the rainy season.

cultural_events.name: Timkat
cultural_events.writeup: Ethiopian Orthodox celebration of Epiphany, featuring colorful processions and religious ceremonies.

wiki.extract: Timkat is an Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church and Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Church celebration of Epiphany. It is celebrated on 19 January, corresponding to the 11th day of Terr in the Ge'ez calendar.

cultural_events.name: Meskel
cultural_events.writeup: Festival commemorating the discovery of the True Cross, marked by bonfires and community gatherings.

wiki.extract: Meskel is an Ethiopian and Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Church holiday that commemorates the discovery of the True Cross by the Roman Empress Saint Helena of Constantinople in the fourth century. Meskel is celebrated by Oriental Orthodox members of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, the Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Church, and to a lesser extent Roman Catholic members of the Ethiopian Catholic Church, the Eritrean Catholic Church, and among Protestant members of P'ent'ay - Ethiopian-Eritrean Evangelicalism. It is a localized version of the Feast of the Cross and occurs on the 17 Meskerem in the Ethiopian calendar. "Meskel" is Amharic for "cross".

cultural_events.name: Enkutatash
cultural_events.writeup: Ethiopian New Year celebrated with music, dancing, and gift-giving in September.

wiki.extract: Enkutatash is a New Year holiday in Ethiopia and Eritrea. It is celebrated on Meskerem 1 on the Ethiopian calendar, which is 11 September according to the Gregorian calendar.

food_writeup: Ethiopian cuisine is known for injera, a sourdough flatbread, served with various spicy stews called wats, often featuring lentils, beef, chicken, or vegetables, reflecting the country's rich agricultural heritage and religious fasting traditions.
brief_history: Ethiopia is one of the oldest nations in the world, with human habitation dating back millions of years. It was home to the ancient Kingdom of Aksum and is notable for resisting colonization, maintaining independence except for a brief Italian occupation. It is the origin of coffee and has a unique Christian tradition dating back to the 4th century.
